name: Goal loop — the outer judge loop
description: OUTER of three levels. One run = one iteration. Everything here is a guard or an actuator; all judgment lives in the orchestrator's prompt one level down. It hands the iteration to orchestrator-turn, then MEASURES THE BAR ITSELF (never trusting the turn's account), and only spends a judge once the bar is green — a red bar short-circuits, because a smart seat on a broken build is the cheapest waste available. Judge says met: commit, push, flip the draft PR to ready, notify, stop. Not met: tail-spawn the next iteration ASYNC and settle, so this run ends while the loop lives. There is NO HUMAN in the loop until the goal passes. Params: goalId, iteration, goalStatement, settleConditions, cwd, barCommand, barCwd, runtimeRoot, paramsFile, maxIterations, sessionId, judgeSessionId, notifyAgent, prNumber, branch.

meta.why: Nesting is correct at this seam (depth 1). The turn is not a loop, so nothing accumulates depth; iteration-to-iteration uses an HTTP tail-spawn instead.
The independent measurement. Reached on an always-edge so a thrown turn is still measured rather than assumed. Costs zero tokens and grounds every decision below it.
core:exec REPORTS, core:gate ACTUATES — a non-zero exit leaves the exec node 'completed', so without this the red path never fires. Red bar means the judge is never reached.

params.schema: {"type":"object","additionalProperties":false,"required":["goalMet","verdict","reason","biggestGap","notInspected"],"properties":{"goalMet":{"type":"boolean","description":"true ONLY if every settle condition is genuinely satisfied"},"verdict":{"type":"string","enum":["APPROVE","ESCALATE"]},"reason":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"biggestGap":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"description":"the single most valuable thing to do next, specific enough to act on"},"notInspected":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"description":"what you could NOT check, and why - the loop acts on your denominator"}}}

meta.why: deepseek-v4-pro via seat-deepseek, a ROUTE PROFILE — cartridges/seat-deepseek/ is a workspace.json and nothing else: no process, no port, not in agentruntime.json, unstartable by construction. This node does NOT message a chat agent and never did: workerProfile is a FILE READ (resolveWorkerProfileEnv reads the profile's env block, keeps the WORKER_PROFILE_ENV_KEYS allowlist, scopes the token to this one spawn, and rewrites the lane to /c/<name>@worker so the traffic is not filed under a conversation). It previously named deepseek-dorian, a chat agent, and that was the defect — not leakage, but that a definition naming a person's conversation READS like it whispers one, which cost multiple agents and one operator a day of re-explanation. Chat agents are Kevin's persistent conversations; an agent has no sense of elapsed time, so a conversation resumed days later has no idea a workflow it never launched is about to speak into it. The ONLY channel from this loop to a chat agent is the agent:notify on completion. Everything else is ephemeral. Still cross-family from the Claude orchestrator (clause 3 independence) but on the claude transport, so reply is the FINAL message only. grok-4.5 was tried first and its NDJSON scrape concatenates narration frames into reply, so the leading token was never the verdict and the fail-closed parser discarded two otherwise-good verdicts. Read-only: a judge that can write can make its own verdict true. Schema-validated (instructor pattern): a non-conforming reply is fed its own validation errors and retried in-session, so an unparseable verdict is RECOVERABLE rather than terminal - the failure that stopped iteration 3 on 2026-08-10.
Reads the schema-validated boolean directly. A lone template resolves to the RAW value with its type preserved, so this is a real boolean, not the string "true".

Commits the loop's work, pushes the branch, and flips the DRAFT PR to ready-for-review. Only reachable once the bar is green AND the judge approved — the PR becomes reviewable exactly when the goal is met, never before.

always:true (agent:notify no-ops on a sync run and this caller is a machine). The message states the branch and lets land report what it DID rather than asserting PR readiness — templates have no conditionals, so a claim that is only true when prNumber is set will ship as a falsehood when it is not. Observed 2026-08-10: "PR # is now READY FOR REVIEW".

params.command: node scripts/goal-loop-note.mjs --cid {{run.correlationId}} --cwd "{{params.cwd}}" --iteration {{params.iteration}} --runtime-root "{{params.runtimeRoot}}" && node scripts/goal-loop-spawn.mjs --workflow goal-loop --params-file "{{params.paramsFile}}" --mode async --set iteration={{params.iteration}} --session "{{nodes.orchestrate.result.sessionId}}" --counter iteration --max {{params.maxIterations}}

meta.why: Bar still red: next iteration, no judge spent. A SEPARATE node from spawn_more because multiple incoming edges AND together — one shared spawn node would silently skip whenever either gate took the other branch. Threads the LIVE iteration via --set: goal-loop-spawn reads its counter from the params FILE, which is static (iteration=1 forever), so without this the counter never climbs past 2, the maxIterations ceiling is inert, and the loop only stops by an accidental 409 when the async spawn races the still-running parent. Verified 2026-08-10 on the first-ever tail-spawn (brake-test-01). NOTE-THEN-SPAWN: goal-loop-note writes this iteration's bar output, judge verdict and source fingerprint into <cwd>/.goal/LOOP-LOG.md BEFORE the child is started, so the child can read it. It always exits 0 — a logging failure must never stop the loop from iterating, which is why && is safe here. --session resumes the orchestrator's own session in the child: the worktree stays the durable memory (compaction can eat a session; the loop must survive that), and continuity is the cache/cost optimisation layered on top, never the thing depended on.

meta.why: Bar green but the judge refused: another iteration. ASYNC tail-spawn, so this run settles and ends while the loop stays alive. Exit 2 is the bar declaring ITSELF broken (fable-5 convention, verified in bar-hollowtide-t001.mjs self-test). It must abort the round and surface, NEVER feed the repair arc: a red bar (exit 1) means fix the sim; a broken bar (exit 2) means fix the INSTRUMENT, and iterating on it burns rounds forever on a fine sim. judge_gate already fails on any non-zero exit; the conditioned edges below split exit-2 (here) from exit-1 (spawn_red).
Single terminal on always-edges from every branch, so the run always resolves exactly one resultNode whichever path fired.
